==Russian==

{{number box|ru|2}}

===Etymology===
{{etymon|ru|:inh|orv:дъва}}
{{word|ru|ine|dwóh₁}}
{{dercat|ru|ine-bsl-pro|ine-pro|inh=2}}
{{inh+|ru|orv|дъва}}, from {{inh|ru|sla-pro|*dъ̏va}}, from {{inh|ru|ine-bsl-pro|*duwō}}, from {{inh|ru|ine-pro|*dwóh₁||two}}.

===Pronunciation===
* {{ru-IPA|два́}}
* {{audio|ru|Ru-два.ogg}}

===Numeral===
{{head|ru|numeral|g=m|g2=n|feminine|две}}

# [[two]] (2)
# ''(mark)'' [[two]] ''(out of five)'', [[poor]]; D mark, D grade
#: {{syn|ru|дво́йка|двоя́к|неудовлетвори́тельно|не́уд|два ба́лла|па́ра}}

====Usage notes====
'' '''два''' '' and '' '''две''' '', when in the [[nominative case]] or [[accusative case]], even in compounds (22, 32, 42, 102, etc.), govern the [[genitive]] of the noun.
:* {{uxi|ru|'''два''' [[мальчик|ма́льчика]]|two boys}}
:* {{uxi|ru|'''две''' [[книга|кни́ги]]|two books|lit=two of a book}}
:* {{uxi|ru|[[пятьдеся́т]] '''два''' [[мальчик|ма́льчика]]|fifty-two boys}}
* ''In the nominative case, all nouns become genitive singular. In the accusative case, animate nouns become genitive plural and inanimate nouns remain in genitive singular.''
:* {{ux|ru|'''Две''' [[собака|соба́ки]], '''два''' [[кот|кота́]], '''две''' [[книга|кни́ги]] [[и]] '''два''' [[журнал|журна́ла]] [[свалиться|свали́лись]] [[с|со]] [[стол|стола́]].|Two dogs, two cats, two books and two journals fell from the table.}} (''"два" transforms all nouns from nominative to genitive singular.'')
:* {{ux|ru|[[я|Я]] [[видеть|ви́жу]] '''двух''' [[собака|соба́к]], '''двух''' [[кот|кото́в]], '''две''' [[книга|кни́ги]] [[и]] '''два''' [[журнал|журна́ла]].|I see two dogs, two cats, two books and two journals.}} (''The verb "вижу" governs accusative case, which for dogs and cats becomes genitive plural.'')
:* {{ux|ru|[[я|Я]] [[скачать|скача́л]] '''два''' [[редактор|редактора]] [[и]] [[пригласить|пригласи́л]] [[на]] [[обе́д]] '''двух''' [[редактор|редакторов]].|I downloaded two editors and invited two editors for lunch.}}
:* {{ux|ru|[[заземлить|Заземли́в]] '''два''' [[проводник|проводника́]], [[эле́ктрик]] [[спасти|спас]] '''двух''' [[проводник|проводнико́в]].|Grounding the two (electrical) conductors, the electrician saved the two (train) conductors.}}
* ''The reason behind the '''genitive singular''' here is that in Old Russian '''''два''''' governed the [[dual]] number, and the old '''nominative dual''' form was the same as the masculine '''genitive singular'''. When the dual number was lost in Russian, the form was reanalyzed as the genitive singular. This was extended to include the numbers ''{{m|ru|три}}'' and ''{{m|ru|четы́ре}}'', and eventually it was applied by analogy to feminine nouns as well.''
* ''While the noun is in the '''genitive singular''' following '''два''' or '''две''', an intervening adjective or adjectival participle will be in the '''genitive plural''' or '''nominative plural''' ''
** ''If два is in nominative case, the adjective will be nominative plural when the noun is feminine''
::* {{ux|ru|Тут '''две''' [[большой|большие]] [[собака|соба́ки]], '''два''' [[большой|больших]] [[кот|кота́]], '''две''' [[большой|большие]] [[звезда|звезды́]] [[и]] '''два''' [[большой|больших]] [[стол|стола́]].|Here are two big dogs, two big cats, two big stars and two big tables.}}
** ''If два is in accusative case, the adjective will be accusative plural (the same as the nominative plural) only if the noun is feminine inanimate.''
::* {{ux|ru|[[я|Я]] [[видеть|ви́жу]] '''двух''' [[большой|больших]] [[собака|соба́к]], '''двух''' [[большой|больших]] [[кот|кото́в]], '''две''' [[большой|большие]] [[звезда|звезды́]] [[и]] '''два''' [[большой|больших]] [[стол|стола́]].|I see two big dogs, two big cats, two big stars and two big tables.}}
** Another way of seeing this is:
:* Nominative feminine is две + nominative plural adjective + genitive singular noun
:* Nominative masculine is два + genitive plural adjective + genitive singular noun.
:* Cases other than nominative and accusative (genitive, dative, instrumental, and prepositional) use plural forms, and agree in number and case with the noun.
:* Accusative animate is the same as the genitive, and accusative inanimate is the same as the nominative.
* {{l|ru|три|Три}} and {{l|ru|четы́ре}} obey the same rules.
